Review of the optimistic session creation feature — the seed/suppress/invalidate-on-echo design is coherent, and the two new data-layer tests cover the important suppression and rollback semantics:

1. packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx (~L1360) — `createSession()`'s resolved value is discarded, only failures are caught — if the server ignores or transforms the client-supplied `id` (older backend, proxy rewrite), it happily creates a *different* session while the local seed keeps the phantom one: the follow-up prompt then fails against a nonexistent session but `createFailed` stays false, so the optimistic tab lingers with no recovery path — capture the response, compare ids, and adopt the server id (or run the rollbackCreate path) on mismatch.
2. packages/tui/src/context/data.tsx (~L1080) — the seeded `SessionInfo` has no title/slug, so the tab and header render untitled until the `session.created` echo lands — consider seeding a provisional title (e.g. first line of the prompt, matching whatever the non-optimistic flow displays) to avoid the visible flicker this feature is otherwise meant to remove.
3. packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx (~L1266) — optimistic path activates only when a `projectID` is resolvable and the submission is a plain prompt — worktree/command/skill/shell keep the synchronous flow (documented, good), but there is no signal distinguishing "optimistic" from "awaiting creation" in the UI during the awaited fallback — if the network stalls, the user gets no intermediate feedback unlike the optimistic path — consider a lightweight pending indicator for parity.
4. Test coverage — data-layer tests are good; missing are the prompt-level flows: create-rejects-with-error (navigation home + draft restore + tab close asserted end-to-end) and the id-mismatch case from point 1 — both guard the most fragile part of this change.

Review of the optimistic prompt submission feature — per-session submission tails preserving admission order across remounts, snapshot-based restore, and dropping the setTimeout navigation hack are all solid improvements:

1. packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx (~L110) — `enqueueSubmit` attaches `.finally` to a tail that can reject (e.g. `data.session.sync` or an API call inside the task throwing), which produces a *derived* rejected promise nobody handles — depending on runtime this surfaces as unhandled-rejection noise every time a queued task throws — end the chain with `.finally(...).catch(() => {})` (or ensure tasks can never reject by wrapping their body).
2. packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx (~L1340) — the old flow surfaced distinct errors ("Failed to commit revert", "Failed to send editor context") *before* mutating any UI state; the background path folds revert-commit, agent/model switches, synthetic context, and the prompt itself into one try whose failure all collapse to "Failed to send prompt" — users diagnosing a stuck revert lose the signal — tag the caught error with a stage label and include it in the toast/message.
3. packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx (~L1330) — `editor.markSelectionSent()` runs at submit time, but on later admission failure `restorePrompt` puts back a snapshot whose editor-context selection is now marked sent and won't re-attach — the restored prompt silently loses its attached selection — either clear the sent-mark on rollback or exclude selections from mark-until-admitted.

Same failure on a **different client and OS** — TUI on macOS, not Electron on Windows — so this does not look Electron-specific.

### Environment

- opencode **1.18.15**, TUI (macOS Terminal), `opencode serve` + TUI
- `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` **does not exist**; the only configured plugin is `opencode-models-discovery`
- Provider: local OpenAI-compatible server (oMLX)

### What happened

An `external_directory` permission for `/tmp/*` was raised. The agent loop blocked. **No prompt was rendered in the TUI.**

```
17:44:59.831Z INFO run=7183b7ed "resolved path" arg=/tmp/glpi-apidb.php
17:44:59.842Z INFO run=7183b7ed evaluated permission=external_directory pattern=/tmp/* action.action=ask
17:44:59.842Z INFO run=7183b7ed asking id=per_0256d10c2001XgyEnqvzFqt7gQ patterns=["/tmp/*"]
```

That is the last line in the log for **any** run, followed by ~9 minutes of nothing — matching your "backend completely idle (zero log lines), not working, not retrying — just waiting".

### Server-side proof the prompt existed while the UI showed nothing

The permission record was live and queryable for the entire stall.

`GET /permission`:

```json
[{"id": "per_0256d10c2001XgyEnqvzFqt7gQ",
  "sessionID": "ses_...",
  "permission": "external_directory",
  "patterns": ["/tmp/*"],
  "always": ["/tmp/*"],
  "tool": {"messageID": "msg_...", "callID": "call_43292d2a"}}]
```

Replying over the API cleared it immediately:

```
POST /permission/per_0256d10c2001XgyEnqvzFqt7gQ/reply   {"reply":"always"}
→ 200 true
```

The session resumed from exactly where it stopped with its 227k-token context intact, and `GET /permission` then returned `[]` — the same "resumed within 2 seconds once someone triggered a response" behavior you describe.

### Why this narrows the cause

In #43196 an analogous stall was traced to a blocking user plugin that prevented `Question.ask` from ever running, so no event was emitted and the TUI "correctly had nothing to render".

**That explanation cannot apply here.** There is no plugin installed, and `Permission.ask` clearly *did* run — the record was present in `GET /permission` throughout. So the server held the state and the client never surfaced it: a genuinely missed or unrendered `permission.asked`, not an un-emitted one.

That makes this a real-world case for Layer 2 of #43300 (TUI recovery polling for missed `question.asked`/`permission.asked`, mirroring the CLI transport's existing `recoverQuestion`). The PR author notes "no other opencode user would hit this without that specific plugin" — this is a no-plugin occurrence of the same invisible-prompt outcome.

### Impact

Indistinguishable from an inference-server hang. We spent a full debugging session pulling apart the local inference server — logs, memory guard, KV cache, scheduler concurrency, network path — before locating the block client-side. Earlier occurrences in the same log stalled up to **35.3 minutes**, and each was "fixed" by restarting the inference server, which silently discarded the run.

A workaround for anyone else hitting this: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<serve-port>/permission` will show the pending request, and `POST /permission/<id>/reply {"reply":"once"}` unblocks the session without losing context.

I looked into this and the interesting part is that it isn't only missing UI — the clear path is broken in two places, so wiring up an "Unarchive" button alone returns HTTP 200 and does nothing. That's probably worth knowing before anyone else picks this up.

**1. `packages/core/src/session/projector.ts`** — `time_archived: info.time.archived` passes `undefined` when the timestamp is cleared, and Drizzle omits `undefined` keys from `.set()`. That means "leave this column alone", not "set NULL", so the row keeps its old archived value.

**2. The session update handler** — the guard is `if (ctx.payload.time?.archived !== undefined)`. A client clearing the field sends `{"time":{}}`, because `JSON.stringify` drops undefined-valued properties, so the guard short-circuits and `setArchived` is never reached.

I've put a fix up as a draft: #43919. It fixes both, adds the restore action (dropdown, command, and `ctrl+a` in the TUI), and makes archived sessions findable via palette search grouped under "Archived" — otherwise the restore action is unreachable, since you can't select a session you can't see.
